stops.note: meant "king"; called out when the king piece was threatened in chess
the term for chess spread into Europe through Arabic-mediated trade and translation
named the move that threatened the king, and by extension any sudden stoppage
broadened from the chess term to "restraint" (1510s), a verification mark (1856), and a written bank order (1798)

current_meaning: a written order to a bank to pay money; also, a mark of verification, or a stoppage or restraint
